title: Installing MongoDB
subtitle: Setting up MongoDB locally and connecting with mongosh
author: KERNAL

whyItExists.problem: Before you can use MongoDB, you need a running server and a way to interact with it. Setting up MongoDB correctly on your OS avoids common connection and authentication issues.
whyItExists.solution: MongoDB provides official installers for all major platforms, plus mongosh (the modern MongoDB Shell) for interactive queries. MongoDB Atlas provides a free cloud cluster that requires zero local installation.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Local installation for full control and offline development. MongoDB Atlas for cloud development, team collaboration, and production deployments.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Don't install MongoDB locally just to try it — MongoDB Atlas free tier gives you a real cluster with no setup. Local install is best when you need offline access or OS-level control.

explainModes.beginner: Installing MongoDB is like installing any other program. Once installed, you start the MongoDB server, then use 'mongosh' (the shell) to type commands to it — like a command prompt for your database.
explainModes.simple: MongoDB has a server (mongod) and a shell (mongosh). You install the server, start it, then use mongosh to run JavaScript commands against your data.
explainModes.standard: MongoDB Community Edition runs as a system service (mongod). You interact with it via mongosh, the Node.js-based interactive shell. MongoDB Atlas provides a free cloud cluster as an alternative to local installation.
explainModes.technical: mongod is the MongoDB server daemon that listens on port 27017 by default. mongosh is a REPL built on Node.js v8 that supports modern JavaScript, async/await, and built-in helper methods. The MongoDB Driver (for Node.js, Python, etc.) connects to mongod via the MongoDB Wire Protocol.
explainModes.deepDive: The MongoDB Wire Protocol is a TCP-based protocol. MongoDB 7.x uses a compressed wire protocol with snappy or zlib. mongosh uses the MongoDB Node.js driver internally. The mongod process manages the WiredTiger storage engine, journal, and network layer. Data files are stored in /var/lib/mongodb (Linux) or C:/data/db (Windows) by default, with one .wt file per collection.

items: MongoDB Atlas (Cloud) — Free tier, zero install, runs in the browser. Best for learning.
Local Install — Full control, works offline. Good for active development.
Docker — Run MongoDB in a container. Best for CI/CD and reproducible environments.

content.text: MongoDB Atlas is the cloud-hosted version of MongoDB. The M0 free tier gives you 512 MB of storage and a fully managed 3-node replica set at no cost. No credit card required.

items: Go to mongodb.com/cloud/atlas and sign up
Create a free M0 cluster (choose any cloud provider and region)
Add your IP address to the IP Access List
Create a database user with a username and password
Click 'Connect' and copy your connection string

content.code:
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew tap mongodb/brew
brew install mongodb-community@7.0
brew services start mongodb-community@7.0

# Ubuntu / Debian Linux
wget -qO - https://www.mongodb.org/static/pgp/server-7.0.asc | sudo apt-key add -
echo "deb [ arch=amd64,arm64 ] https://repo.mongodb.org/apt/ubuntu jammy/mongodb-org/7.0 multiverse" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mongodb-org-7.0.list
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y mongodb-org
sudo systemctl start mongod
sudo systemctl enable mongod  # auto-start on boot

# Windows: Download the .msi installer from
# https://www.mongodb.com/try/download/community

# Start MongoDB in Docker with persistent data
docker run -d \
  --name mongodb \
  -p 27017:27017 \
  -e MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME=admin \
  -e MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD=password \
  -v mongodb_data:/data/db \
  mongo:7.0

# Verify it's running
docker ps

# Stop and remove
docker stop mongodb && docker rm mongodb

content.text: mongosh is the official MongoDB Shell — a modern, Node.js-based REPL that supports full JavaScript including async/await. Install it separately from the MongoDB server.

content.code:
# Install mongosh
npm install -g mongosh          # via npm
brew install mongosh             # macOS

# Connect to local MongoDB
mongosh
# or explicitly
mongosh "mongodb://localhost:27017"

# Connect to Atlas
mongosh "mongodb+srv://username:password@cluster.mongodb.net/mydb"

# Connect to Docker MongoDB
mongosh "mongodb://admin:password@localhost:27017" --authenticationDatabase admin

content.text: mongosh is a full JavaScript environment — you can use variables, loops, and async/await. Try: const result = await db.users.findOne(); console.log(result.name)
On a fresh local install, MongoDB has NO authentication enabled. Never deploy to production without enabling authentication. See the Security lesson for how to secure MongoDB.

content.title: Simulate mongosh Commands

questions.question: What is mongosh?
questions.explanation: mongosh is the MongoDB Shell — a Node.js-based interactive JavaScript REPL for running MongoDB commands.

questions.question: What is the default port MongoDB listens on?
questions.explanation: MongoDB listens on port 27017 by default. This is the standard MongoDB port used by all drivers and tools.

questions.question: Which command in mongosh switches to a database called 'myapp'?
questions.explanation: The 'use <database>' command in mongosh switches to that database (and creates it lazily on first insert).

faq.q: How do I connect to Atlas from mongosh?
faq.a: Use mongosh with the connection string from the Atlas Connect dialog, e.g. mongosh "mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster.mongodb.net/mydb". You can find this string in your Atlas cluster's 'Connect' dialog under 'Connect with the MongoDB Shell'.

faq.q: What is the difference between mongod and mongosh?
faq.a: mongod is the MongoDB database server process — it manages data files and listens for connections. mongosh is the client shell you use to send commands to mongod. You need mongod running before you can connect with mongosh.

faq.q: Should I use MongoDB Atlas or install locally?
faq.a: For learning and small projects, Atlas free tier (M0) is the easiest path — no installation, automatic backups, and free forever. For production, Atlas provides managed infrastructure. Install locally only when you need offline access or OS-level control over the database.
